en-US.author: Cognition AI, Inc.
en-US.description: A fast and minimal agent that lives both in your terminal and in the cloud.
en-US.name: Devin CLI
en-US.releaseNotes:
Added
- /vim turns on Vim editing in the prompt box. Press Esc for Normal mode to navigate by word, edit text objects, or select text in Visual mode.
- Pin a model with Alt+P in /model. Pinned models appear first, and Alt+N cycles through them without reopening the picker.
- Set permission_mode in /config to choose the starting mode for new local sessions. --permission-mode overrides it for one launch.
- devin mcp list --json lists configured MCP servers and their enabled state, transport, and disabled tools.
- Paste clipboard images on Windows with Alt+V; in WSL, use Ctrl+V or Alt+V.

Changed
- /resume shows each session’s project and age. Search by project name, or press Alt+G to switch between the current directory and all projects, ordered by last activity.
- In a tool approval prompt, press 1 for Once, 2 for Session, 3 for Project, or 4 for Always.
- /clear lets you type immediately and queues your prompt until the new session is ready.
- ContextInput hooks can observe relayed text such as subagent reports.
- PostToolUse hooks get the path to the complete output when a tool result is truncated.

Fixed
- Plan approvals now show the plan summary and file path before you decide.
- Ensured UserPromptSubmit hooks run when a task is transferred via /handoff.
- Changes saved in /config take effect on /clear, /resume, or /cloud without restarting the CLI.
- Sending a follow-up while an edit awaits approval no longer leaves the session stuck without approval buttons.
- Accept Edits and Smart mode now recognize workspace edits on Windows network shares, including WSL folders.
- The CLI no longer loses config changes saved in quick succession, such as pinning two models.
- Images that cannot be decoded no longer cause the whole turn to fail.
- devin -p now continues to an answer after denying a tool call that would need interactive approval.
- The CLI warns and keeps running if it cannot create its log file. PowerShell command output on Windows now preserves non-ASCII characters.
